identity: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam Philosophy, English-taught track, full-time annual example for 2026–2027. The normalized target includes a part-time option, which follows a different pace and does not alter the comparator credit weight. Dutch track and its Plus variants remain separate.
ledger: The English language test or a completed refresher is required before the grade can be awarded.
Philosophy in the Global Middle Ages
Includes the Broader Mind certificate within the 6 EC course.
Close reading of Plato’s Sophist in the published course.
Close reading of Kant’s Critique of Pure Reason in the published course.
World Philosophies and the Construction of Traditions I
This elective satisfies the requirement to take World Philosophies I or II.
The published elective focuses on pragmatism.
Open minor, approved electives or study abroad
Students choose a minor, approved electives or study abroad. Individual electives include at least 12 EC at level 300.
Students prepare a thesis proposal, develop arguments and give peer feedback.
A 12 EC individual thesis. Entry requires all first-year courses and 48 EC from year two.
The published elective studies Platonism and Neoplatonism.
progression: The adopted English Philosophy annual plan has ten required 6 EC first-year units, eight required and two selected 6 EC second-year units, and 30 EC of open study, two 6 EC philosophy choices, a 6 EC thesis seminar and a 12 EC thesis. The example selects Theoretical Philosophy and World Philosophies I in year two, and Contemporary Ethics and History of Philosophy in year three. The World Philosophies I/II condition is met once. Both first-year and second-year Philosophical Encounters seminars carry zero credits, as does the English language test. The test or completed refresher gates Academic English. The binding study recommendation requires 42 first-year EC and the language quality requirement. Political Philosophy includes a Broader Mind certificate. The thesis requires all first-year courses and 48 second-year EC, and is assessed by two readers. Open study has level, approval and non-overlap rules. The distinct Dutch Philosophy Plus routes do not enter this example.
interestAccounting: All 84 owned rows, two separately mapped source groups of 42, were reviewed. Repeated interests were accounted for individually without treating duplication as added disciplinary weight.

interests.text: fundamental questions about people, organisations and countries
interests.assessment: Fundamental reasoning about persons and institutions is taught in ethics and political philosophy.

interests.text: critical reflection on science, culture, religion and society
interests.assessment: The breadth is genuine, with distinct philosophical questions across disciplines. Religious content does not imply an English theology track.

interests.text: philosophical approaches to current social issues
interests.assessment: Contemporary social questions recur as applications of normative reasoning.

interests.text: how to respond to major challenges
interests.assessment: The political-philosophy course applies arguments and perspectives to public challenges.

interests.text: whether individual choices contribute to climate change
interests.assessment: Climate responsibility is an application of the stable practical philosophy direction. The English Political Philosophy course names climate debate.

interests.text: the ethics and politics of free markets
interests.assessment: Markets are an application of ethics and political philosophy, supported in UCR by introductory economic mechanisms.

interests.text: whether argument can change someone’s mind
interests.assessment: Argument and public debate are explicitly taught.
Formal reasoning and argument reconstruction provide direct foundations.

interests.text: philosophy across history from antiquity to the present
interests.assessment: The annual history sequence ranges from antiquity to contemporary philosophy.
Broader Mind connects philosophical arguments to current questions with students from other disciplines.
The general English track is the exact selected route.

interests.text: philosophy combined with religion and theology
interests.assessment: A real Dutch Philosophy Plus variant, outside the selected English route.

interests.text: philosophy combined with governance and organisation
interests.assessment: The formal Dutch governance variant is separate. English political philosophy independently supports public reasoning.
A stable area within the English route, with narrower historical coverage at UCR.
A stable area, developed in the climate/public ethics alternative.
A stable area, represented by mind, agency, logic and philosophical essays. Further direction would largely reuse those courses.

Social Philosophy is required and remains a discrete gap.

interests.assessment: Epistemology is required. General empirical methodology is complementary.
Propositions and quantifiers overlap. Natural deduction and philosophy of logic are deeper VU emphases.
Argumentation is required. Rhetoric provides a partial methodological overlap.

interests.text: ancient philosophy in a global perspective
interests.assessment: Global Antiquity includes multiple philosophical traditions. UCR addresses some Greek arguments.

interests.text: medieval philosophy in a global perspective
interests.assessment: Global Middle Ages remains a distinct historical requirement.
Modern Philosophy is a dedicated requirement, with broader historical context at UCR.

Intercultural Philosophy and Postcolonial Theory remains a distinct requirement.
History of Analytic Philosophy is a required historical course, separate from formal Logic.
Political Philosophy supports rights, ideologies and public reasoning.
Philosophy of Science is required; disciplinary science and methods do not replace it.
Free will and personal identity overlap with UCR. VU also treats modality, ontology and composition.

interests.assessment: Close reading is central. Literature and philosophical essays offer partial skill development.

interests.assessment: Governance and technology is Dutch-variant support.
